headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Firecrawl’s broad egress can expose Khoj-indexed notes and API keys if paired without isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes scrape/interact APIs, while Khoj retrieves and chats over indexed documents. If Firecrawl output is copied into Khoj or indexed into shared notes, attacker-controlled content can become trusted instructions. No shared channel is documented, so this is an inferred but plausible default-pathway risk.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is imported into Khoj notes or chat context without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge is used between the agents, attacker-controlled web text can reach Khoj.
mitigations: Disable automatic import of scraped text into Khoj.
Add a prompt-injection filter before indexing Firecrawl output.
Use a separate staging note for reviewed content only.
Mark web-scraped content as untrusted in Khoj prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from Firecrawl to Khoj retrieval.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, structured data, and API keys and has broad network egress; Khoj indexes personal notes and documents and can also use broad egress. If they share a workspace or the same account context, sensitive notes or keys can be exfiltrated through Firecrawl’s outbound requests. The pairwise pathway is not directly documented, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF Firecrawl is pointed at a directory or source containing Khoj-indexed notes, those contents can leave the system.
IF both agents operate under the same user workspace or credentials, sensitive data can flow from Khoj into Firecrawl outputs or requests.
mitigations: Keep Firecrawl and Khoj on separate workspaces.
Exclude notes and secrets from Firecrawl inputs.
Rotate any API keys already indexed by Khoj.
Restrict Firecrawl egress to approved domains.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage and network isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad egress, while Khoj supports multiple instances with shared index across clients but cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. There is overlap in mutable shared state only if the same indexed corpus is targeted, but the profiles do not show direct write-write contention. This is a limited coordination risk, not a strong conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to update the same shared index or corpus concurrently, stale or conflicting entries may occur.
IF an operator uses Firecrawl to regenerate content while Khoj reindexes the same source at the same time, race conditions can appear.
mitigations: Schedule reindexing windows.
Pause Khoj ingestion during Firecrawl crawls.
Use separate source folders per agent.
Check for duplicate or stale entries after sync.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared index updates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped content and structured data, and Khoj is a retrieval/chat system that can surface indexed documents as answers. If Khoj treats Firecrawl output as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinated facts can cascade into downstream decisions. The pair is not documented as integrated, so this is inferred from their default workflows.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is indexed into Khoj without human review, incorrect facts can be repeated as trusted answers.
IF Khoj is used to brief operators or trigger follow-on actions, a single bad scrape can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before indexing scraped content.
Add source citations to Khoj answers.
Flag Firecrawl-derived notes as unverified.
Compare scraped facts against a second source.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles web content and API keys, while Khoj stores personal notes and indexed documents. If EU personal data or secrets are scraped into Khoj and then sent through Firecrawl’s broad egress or external search providers, retention and residency obligations can diverge. No specific certifications or residency guarantees are documented, so the safer medium classification applies.
conditions: IF EU personal data is indexed in Khoj and then exported through Firecrawl or external search providers, residency obligations may be violated.
IF secrets or regulated notes are stored in Khoj and scraped by Firecrawl, retention and access controls may diverge.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows.
Separate EU and non-EU datasets.
Review retention settings for both systems.
Redact secrets before crawling or indexing.
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-processing agreements and residency controls.
